The paper provides non-trivial lower bounds on convex performance metrics of scattered fields for absorptionless electromagnetic devices.
Direct application of Lagrangian duality without field constraints yields trivial bounds.
Introducing a norm constraint on the electric field inside the device resolves the triviality issue.
The field constraint is expressed as ||E - E_ref|| ≤ α ||E_ref||, where E_ref is a reference field.
The dual problem with the field constraint can be formulated as a convex conic optimization problem.
The bounding procedure is demonstrated on 2D scattering problems with circular design regions.
For transverse-electric polarization, the scattering cross-section upper bound increases with the contrast χ and design radius R.
For transverse-magnetic polarization, the scattering cross-section can be unbounded if negative permittivity materials are allowed.
The parameter α depends on the design region, background Green's function, and contrast limits.
The method uses the Green's function of the background permittivity distribution to relate fields and currents.
The scattering cross-section is expressed as f[Φ] = 2 Im <E_inc, Φ>, a convex function of the polarization current Φ.
Numerical discretization uses pulse-basis and delta-testing functions with spatial resolution δx = λ/100.
Local optimization results closely match the bounds for small contrasts and small design regions.
The bounding technique can be integrated with existing methods for absorptive electromagnetic devices to improve bounds.
The approach is general and can be extended to wave scattering problems in acoustics and quantum physics.
The paper includes a supplementary section detailing the dual problem derivation and numerical convergence.
The field norm constraint parameter α has an explicit upper bound formula involving operator norms of Green's functions and contrast parameters.
For large contrast or large design regions, the field norm constraint α can diverge, limiting the bounding procedure's applicability.
The bounding procedure reveals that superscattering effects in lossless metallic nanoparticles are consistent with unbounded scattering cross-sections.
